action_trace.summary: Generated 8 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (query performance, error clarity), pain points (unbounded sorts, type resolution friction), and acceptance criteria (solution presentation, prioritization) for ES|QL sort handling, First/Last aliases, and vector dispatch optimization within the elasticsearch_2026q1 case.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (unbounded sort clarity, alias handling), pain points (command attribution, debugging difficulty), and acceptance criteria (prioritization framework, edge cases). Questions decompose requirement fragments into user-centric concerns addressing ES|QL sorting transparency, post-preview feature completion, and vector dispatch behavior.

Generated 10 targeted interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (clear error messaging, post-tech-preview feature prioritization), pain points (unbounded sort identification, vector operation complexity), and acceptance criteria (explicit command attribution, solution suggestions, success metrics). Questions decompose the requirement fragments into actionable user needs across error clarity, alias functionality, and vector dispatch behavior.

End users need explicit, actionable error messages identifying problematic ES|QL commands with remediation guidance; First/Last function consistency for SQL-migration scenarios; and transparent vectorization behavior to enable confident query optimization in business analytics workflows.

End users require explicit command attribution and actionable remediation guidance in ES|QL error messages, particularly for multi-value operations causing sort constraint violations. Deferred post-tech-preview work on aliases/types and vector optimization must be clearly communicated with performance and scope implications.

End users require explicit command attribution and actionable remediation guidance in ES|QL error messages when operations like MV_EXPAND cause unbounded sort constraints. Current cryptic diagnostics force time-consuming manual investigation in complex queries; enhanced error clarity with command naming and step-by-step solutions will significantly reduce debugging overhead and improve analyst productivity.

Clarification needed on error message specificity (line numbers, operation sequences), scope of remediation guidance, command attribution in multi-step queries, comprehensive list of constraint-violating commands, and whether preventive validation tooling should be included in the solution.

EndUser raises five clarification questions to disambiguate error message design for ES|QL unbounded sort constraints. Key concerns: (1) precision of command location in queries, (2) definition and scope of remediation guidance, (3) error attribution logic for multi-step operations, (4) consistency across constraint types, and (5) optimal contextual information for analyst debugging efficiency.

EndUser raises six critical clarification questions addressing error message specificity (line numbers vs. sequence position), remediation guidance scope (examples vs. suggestions vs. links), attribution logic (direct vs. indirect causation), UX trade-offs, complexity-based formatting, and whether optimization constraints should be exposed in diagnostics. These questions resolve ambiguities in Requirement 4 (Issue #140103) regarding ES|QL command attribution and error clarity for unbounded sort constraints.

End-user confirms requirement for explicit command attribution in ES|QL error messages with actionable remediation steps. Refines that errors must include line numbers and operation sequence positions, and distinguish direct vs. indirect constraint causes. Identifies critical pain point of multi-step query debugging requiring enhanced diagnostic clarity.

End-user validation confirms that ES|QL error messaging for unbounded sort constraints requires: explicit command naming, dual-location error attribution (line number + operation sequence), three-part remediation guidance (examples, alternatives, documentation), and distinction between direct/indirect causation. Target users are data analysts requiring rapid debugging feedback to reduce query development time from hours to minutes.

End-user requirements for Elasticsearch 2026Q1 ES|QL error messaging are validated and refined: error messages must explicitly name problematic commands with dual-location context (line number + sequence position), provide three-part remediation guidance (examples, alternatives, documentation), and distinguish between direct causes and contributing factors in multi-step queries to significantly reduce debugging time and improve developer experience.

Consolidated 5 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue addressing ES|QL error message clarity (explicit command naming with dual-location attribution), actionable remediation guidance (3-component structure), command attribution scope (direct vs. indirect causation), and deferred tech-preview work items. All requirements validated against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 documentation standards with confirmed pain-point alignment and deployment impact assessment.

Five prioritized user requirements synthesized from Elasticsearch Q1 2026 interview data: three MUST-priority requirements addressing ES|QL error message clarity, command attribution, and remediation guidance (reducing debugging time from hours to minutes); one SHOULD-priority requirement for post-tech-preview First/Last aliases implementation; one COULD-priority enhancement for error context visualization. All requirements validated through enduser confirmations and traceable to interview records IR-ES26Q1-001 through IR-ES26Q1-005.

Seven targeted deployment-focused questions probe infrastructure synchronicity constraints, security implications of exposing query structure in errors, scalability of multi-operation attribution logic, performance budgets for metadata management, integration requirements across downstream systems, vector-dispatch transparency in error attribution, and infrastructure readiness for deferred tech-preview functionality—grounded in MoSCoW prioritization and life-cycle trade-off reasoning.

Eight targeted questions probe infrastructure constraints (parse/execution timing, metadata persistence, client integration), security mandates (query structure disclosure, content governance), scalability thresholds (command attribution cost, deferred feature implementation), and operational requirements (versioning, MTTR validation). Questions bridge requirements REQ-ES26Q1-001 through REQ-ES26Q1-004 and ground dialogue in deployment realities.

Probing Deployer on error message infrastructure (pipeline architecture, latency budgets, schema compatibility), security implications (query exposure in logs/caches, audit requirements), scalability trade-offs (command attribution complexity at 50+ operations, remediation example generation strategy), and deployment sequencing for both immediate error clarity enhancements and deferred post-tech-preview vector/alias functionality.

Deployer confirms infrastructure capacity for sub-100ms error generation with AST metadata preservation (2-5% memory overhead), security-hardened remediation guidance from templated documentation, 10K+ event/sec scalability with feature-flag support for First/Last aliases, operational audit logging with command causation chains, and tiered error detail levels for cost optimization. Dual-location attribution (line + sequence) and graceful degradation during cluster failures are critical for production reliability.

Deployer constraints establish sub-100ms error latency via local catalog caching, mandate AST preservation (2-5% memory overhead) for dual-location attribution, require content sanitization for security, target horizontal scalability to 1000+ nodes, and implement circuit breaker fallback patterns. Operational procedures include audit logging (90-day retention), hot-reload templates, and stateless design eliminating additional infrastructure cost. Security mandates redact sensitive data while preserving command attribution; cost optimization achieves 15-20% traffic reduction with zero additional infrastructure.

Deployer constraints for elasticsearch_2026q1 ES|QL error messaging: sub-100ms latency via node-local caching, AST preservation (2-5% memory overhead), dual-location attribution, content sanitization for security, horizontal scalability to 10K+ concurrent queries, hot-reload catalog updates, and tiered caching strategy targeting 95% hit ratio. Requires distributed cache invalidation, stateless service design, and monitoring for latency/sanitization compliance.

Deployer requires 7 critical clarifications on latency-memory trade-offs for AST preservation, error catalog synchronization strategy, security-actionability balance in remediation examples, vectorization conflicts, and resource allocation for deferred post-tech-preview work before confirming deployment feasibility for elasticsearch_2026q1 error message enhancement requirements.

Six clarifications needed to resolve deployment feasibility: (1) latency-memory trade-off acceptance criteria for AST preservation, (2) AST caching strategy (always-on vs. opt-in vs. lazy), (3) security-actionability balance for sanitized remediation examples, (4) distributed cache synchronization and staleness handling, (5) Q1 2026 resource allocation and dependency sequencing for post-tech-preview work, (6) vector-only dispatch feature scope clarification. Chain-of-thought: infrastructure constraints create performance-security-functionality triangle requiring explicit priority decisions before implementation can proceed.

Deployer requires 5 critical clarifications on infrastructure trade-offs (latency vs. AST overhead), operational strategy (AST preservation scope), security-functional tension (sanitization vs. remediation examples), distributed deployment implications, and tech preview item prioritization (First/Last aliases optimization dependencies). Chain-of-Thought analysis reveals conflicts between sub-100ms latency mandate and 2-5% memory overhead; sanitization security controls and concrete example requirements; and unclear vectorization prerequisite status. Resolution required before implementation planning.

Deployer role validates three critical deployment tensions: (1) latency vs. AST overhead—resolved by separating infrastructure prerequisites from latency SLAs; (2) security vs. actionability—resolved via tiered sanitization preserving command names while redacting sensitive values; (3) scope clarity—confirms error message enhancement focus with First/Last aliases descoped to Q2. Requires capacity planning review and cluster state convergence validation before production deployment.

Deployer role confirms deployment feasibility for elasticsearch_2026q1 requirements with three critical refinements: (1) latency requirement applies to error construction only, not AST overhead; (2) always-on AST preservation operationalized as standard pipeline behavior with optimized 0.5-1% memory overhead via execution frame stack; (3) tiered sanitization implemented to preserve command/constraint details while redacting sensitive data. Infrastructure constraints validated; security and scalability trade-offs accepted. Deployment-ready pending vector-only dispatch coordination for deferred tech preview items.

Deployer role confirms infrastructure strategy for elasticsearch_2026q1 error messaging enhancement. Key decisions: (1) Separate latency requirement from AST memory overhead to enable dual-location attribution without latency penalty; (2) Always-on AST preservation for consistency across distributed deployments; (3) Tiered sanitization preserving actionability while preventing information disclosure; (4) Local error catalog caching achieves sub-100ms target with minimal footprint. Three MUST requirements (REQ-ES26Q1-001/002/003) deployment-ready; SHOULD requirement (004) deferred to capacity planning; COULD requirement (005) backlogged for future iteration. Deployment validated against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 checklist with infrastructure, security, and cost trade-offs confirmed.

Operating environment specification for Elasticsearch 2026Q1 ES|QL error attribution system requires: (1) hardware supporting 2-5% memory overhead for AST preservation; (2) distributed network with sub-100ms error generation latency via local node caching; (3) compute infrastructure maintaining complete query context through execution; (4) tiered security sanitization protecting sensitive data while preserving actionable remediation details; (5) always-on AST preservation strategy for consistent multi-location error attribution across clusters.

Consolidated 10-item system requirements list (IEEE 830 format) for elasticsearch_2026q1 addressing ES|QL error message clarity, dual-location command attribution, actionable remediation guidance, AST preservation, distributed latency optimization, tiered sanitization, and post-tech-preview First/Last aliases evaluation. Requirements reconcile user pain points (debugging time reduction), deployer constraints (sub-100ms latency, 2-5% memory overhead, security sanitization), and operational environment specifications (distributed caching, AST pipeline preservation).
